# nori

> nori is a scrolling window manager for macOS, modeled on niri. Windows stand side by side as columns on a horizontal strip, one strip per Space. This file tells an assistant how to help someone configure it. Everything nori can be configured with is listed here; if a setting isn't here, it doesn't exist, so say so instead of inventing one.

## How to help

1. Ask what the person wants to change, or read their current `~/.config/nori/config.toml` if they paste it.
2. Give back the whole edited file, or only the lines to add, with a comment on each changed line.
3. Tell them to save it and choose "Reload Config" (⌘R) in nori's menu bar item, or run `nori reload`. Mistakes don't crash nori: it prints a warning to stderr, skips that line and applies the rest.

The menu item "Open Config" opens the file, and creates it with every setting and its default if it's missing. `~/.config/nori/config.default.toml` (menu item "Show All Settings") always holds every setting of the installed version with its default and a comment; nori rewrites it on every start and never reads it. "Settings…" (⌘,) edits the same settings, bindings and rules in a window, applies each change at once and writes it into config.toml without touching the rest, so the person can also do it there instead.

## The file

TOML, read by nori's own small parser. It knows comments, plain keys, `"strings"`, `'literal strings'`, numbers, `true`, `false`, `[tables]` and `[[arrays of tables]]`. It skips dotted or quoted keys, arrays, inline tables, multi-line strings and dates. So write every rule as its own `[[rule]]` table, never `rules = [...]` or `{ app = ... }`.

```toml
gap = 16                  # between windows, in points
padding-top = 40          # from the menu bar
padding-bottom = 0        # from the Dock or the bottom of the screen
padding-left = 24
padding-right = 24
resize-step = 10          # Opt+= / Opt+- width step, % of screen width
launch-at-login = false   # add Nori.app to Login Items (only the app bundle, move it to /Applications first)
overview-background = "none"  # behind the overview's Spaces: "none" (black) or "blur" (the wallpaper, blurred, dimmed 30%)
center-focused-column = "always"     # "always": focused window in the center; "never": scroll only to show it whole;
                                     # "on-overflow": center it only when it doesn't fit beside the window focus came from
always-center-single-column = false  # true: a lone window in the center whatever center-focused-column says
wrap-around = false       # true: focus-left on the first column goes to the last, focus-space-up on the first Space to the last
inactive-opacity = 1.0    # 0.1 to 1: the strip's unfocused windows are shown at this opacity, the focused one opaque; 1 turns it off
mouse-modifier = "option" # modifiers held for a left drag (move a window) or right drag (resize it); e.g. "ctrl+option"

[bindings]                          # "none" unbinds an action
focus-left = "option+h"             # focus the column to the left / right
focus-right = "option+l"
focus-first = "ctrl+option+h"       # focus the first / last column
focus-last = "ctrl+option+l"
focus-space-down = "option+j"       # go to the Space below / above
focus-space-up = "option+k"
center-column = "option+c"          # scroll the focused window to the center, whatever center-focused-column says
overview = "option+o"
show-floating = "option+f"          # windows outside the strip (floating rules, dialogs, PiP) above it, focus stays
toggle-floating = "option+shift+v"  # focused window out of the strip, floating in the middle, and back
grow-width = "option+="
shrink-width = "option+-"
cycle-width-forward = "option+."    # focused window to the next wider of 1/3, 1/2, 2/3 of the screen
cycle-width-backward = "option+,"   # … to the next narrower
toggle-full-width = "option+shift+f"  # full width, and back
move-left = "option+shift+h"        # move the focused window one column left
move-right = "option+shift+l"
move-to-space-down = "option+shift+j"  # send the focused window to the Space below / above
move-to-space-up = "option+shift+k"
move-to-space-1 = "option+shift+1"  # send the focused window to Desktop 1; move-to-space-1 … move-to-space-9

[[rule]]
app = "Telegram"
space = 3
```

Top-level keys are only `gap`, `padding-top`, `padding-bottom`, `padding-left`, `padding-right`, `resize-step`, `inactive-opacity` (numbers), `launch-at-login`, `always-center-single-column` and `wrap-around` (true/false, default false), `overview-background` ("none" or "blur", default "none"), `center-focused-column` ("always", "never" or "on-overflow", default "always") and `mouse-modifier` (modifiers joined by `+`, default "option"). A missing number is 0, except `resize-step`, which is 10, and `inactive-opacity`, which is 1.

## Bindings

The only bindable actions are the ones in the `[bindings]` block above: `focus-left`, `focus-right`, `focus-first`, `focus-last`, `focus-space-down`, `focus-space-up`, `center-column`, `overview`, `show-floating`, `toggle-floating`, `grow-width`, `shrink-width`, `cycle-width-forward`, `cycle-width-backward`, `toggle-full-width`, `move-left`, `move-right`, `move-to-space-down`, `move-to-space-up` and `move-to-space-1` … `move-to-space-9`. A missing one keeps its default; `"none"` unbinds it. Every action is also a CLI command (`nori focus left`, `nori move space up`, `nori width toggle-full`, `nori center`, `nori overview`, `nori show floating`, see `nori help`), for people who drive nori from Raycast, Hammerspoon or a bar.

A binding is modifiers and one key joined by `+`, like `"ctrl+shift+1"`. Modifiers: `option` (or `alt`, `opt`), `ctrl` (or `control`), `cmd` (or `command`), `shift`. The key is one letter `a`–`z`, a digit `0`–`9`, `-`, `=`, `,`, `.`, `left`, `right`, `up` or `down`. No function keys, space, return or other punctuation. Keys are physical keys on the US layout, so a binding stays put when the person switches keyboard layouts. One chord per action: an action can't have two keys.

These keys are fixed and can't be rebound in the config:

- Opt+1…5 are macOS's own "Switch to Desktop N" shortcuts. Change them in System Settings → Keyboard → Keyboard Shortcuts → Mission Control. nori needs those shortcuts on.
- Left drag with `mouse-modifier` held moves a window, right drag resizes it. Only the modifier is configurable, not the buttons.
- Trackpad: three fingers sideways scroll the strip, three fingers up/down switch Spaces, four fingers open the overview.

## App rules

One `[[rule]]` table per app, or several with a `title`. `app` is the app's name or bundle id, in any case. `title` is optional: a regular expression (NSRegularExpression syntax) the window's title must contain, case-insensitive. The first rule that matches a window wins, and one rule can combine actions. A rule needs `app` and at least one action (`space`, `floating`, `ignore` or `width`), or nori skips it.

```toml
[[rule]]
app = "Telegram"
space = 3              # new Telegram windows go to Desktop 3

[[rule]]
app = "com.apple.finder"
floating = true        # windows stay out of the strip; nori doesn't move or resize them

[[rule]]
app = "Raycast"
ignore = true          # nori neither moves nor lists the app's windows

[[rule]]
app = "Ghostty"
width = 50             # a new window takes 50 % of the usable width; the gap is counted in, so 50 + 50 fill the screen

[[rule]]
app = "Safari"
title = "Picture in Picture"
floating = true        # only Safari windows with that title float; put a plain app = "Safari" rule after it for the rest
```

- `space = N`, a whole number from 1. Desktops count from 1 across all displays, like the system shortcuts. nori moves each window once, the first time it sees it, including windows already open at start. Moved back by hand, it stays.
- `floating = true` suits apps whose main windows shouldn't be columns: calculators, color pickers, small utilities. Dialogs, panels, sheets and browser popups already stay out of the strip without a rule.
- `ignore = true` suits launchers, menu bar apps and overlays. Raycast, Alfred, Spotlight and LaunchBar are ignored already, no rule needed; a rule in the config for one of them takes precedence.
- `width = N`, a number over 0 up to 100, percent of the usable width. Applied once, when the window joins the strip; a later resize by hand or key stays.
- `title` rules need the title: nori reads it through Accessibility on the current Space, and on other Spaces only with Screen Recording permission. A window without a readable title doesn't match a title rule and falls through to the next rule.
- On reload, changed `floating` and `ignore` rules apply to open windows at once. A new `space` or `width` rule only affects windows nori hasn't seen yet.

To find an app's exact name or bundle id, the person can run (with the `nori` CLI linked onto PATH, `ln -s /Applications/Nori.app/Contents/MacOS/nori /opt/homebrew/bin/nori`):

```sh
nori query windows | jq -r '.[] | "\(.app)\t\(.bundleId)"' | sort -u
```

or `osascript -e 'id of app "AppName"'`.

## Not configurable

Animation speed and curves, gestures, the number of fingers, column widths other than `resize-step`, the fixed 1/3, 1/2, 2/3 presets and a rule's `width`, multiple displays (nori uses the main one), several windows per column. Don't offer settings for these.

## More

README: https://github.com/freethinkel/nori#readme. It also covers setup (SIP, boot argument, Accessibility), the CLI and limitations.
